title: SLA-sensitive rollout runbook and customer impact matrix (Mar 2026) - draft
content:
Purpose:
This runbook describes a rollout pattern for changes that are SLA-sensitive (p99 latency targets, tiered customer SLAs, and region-locked traffic). It bundles an hourly rollout calendar, a lightweight preflight checklist, a telemetry sampling plan, a customer-impact matrix, and a release-notes draft to be shared with CS/AM preflight. The intent: minimize customer-visible risk and provide clear, fast rollback decisions when SLOs deviate.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to API surface changes and model variant switches that can affect per-token latency and error rates.
- Traffic can be routed by region and by customer tier (standard, enterprise, platinum).
- Expected baseline: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 400ms on Dedicated fleet.
- Canary traffic will be < 1% initially and ramp via automated schedule.

Preflight checklist (complete 24–2 hours before T0):
- [ ] Release artifacts built and pinned (docker images, model hashes). Link: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/876.
- [ ] Smoke tests green on staging for the same config and model seed. Attach logs.
- [ ] Canary control plane config staged in Canary namespace with exact routing rules.
- [ ] Rollout policy created: ramp steps, throttle thresholds, automatic fallback model variant.
- [ ] Alerting hooks prepared: daily and hourly SLO monitors, error budget burn alarm, customer-impact channel #cs-impact.
- [ ] CS/AM notified with proposed rollout calendar and draft release notes (this doc).
- [ ] Runbook owner and on-call rotation assigned (owner + 2 deputies).

SLA-sensitive hourly rollout calendar (T0 = release open window start):
- T-24: Final preflight signoff email to stakeholders (CS, SRE, Product).
- T-4: Production config pushed to canary namespace (no traffic).
- T-2: Canary smoke sequence executed (minimal synthetic L1 flows).
- T-0 (00:00): Start canary at 0.5% globally, but restricted for platinum customers routed to fallback lane (0% exposure). Observe 30m.
- T+0:30: If p99 latency delta <= +15% and error rate delta <= +0.05% vs baseline, increase to 2% for 30m. Else, roll back to previous model and notify stakeholders.
- T+1:00: If stable, increase to 5% for 30m with focused telemetry sampling for enterprise customers.
- T+1:30: If stable, increase to 15% for 1h (standard tier) but still keep platinum on fallback.
- T+2:30: Expand to 40% for 2h (regional gating: EU/NA only). Monitor regional p99 and per-customer 95th percentile.
- T+4:30: Full region expansion (70%) for 3h if SLOs hold; begin staggered lift for platinum (10% test exposure).
- T+7:30: Full rollout if all gates pass and error budget impact is within threshold. Final go/no-go signoff by release owner and SRE lead.

Fast rollback decision criteria (automated and manual):
Automated rollback triggers:
- Sustained p99 latency above baseline + 30% for 15 minutes.
- Error rate spike: increase of > 0.5% absolute for 10 minutes.
- Rate limiter saturation or queue growth > 3x baseline across serving runtime nodes.
Manual rollback triggers:
- Any customer-reported incident from enterprise/platinum tiers with confirmed degradation.
- Stepwise failure to clear health checks during ramp step.
Rollback actions:
1) Pause ramp and shift traffic back to previous model variant for affected shards/regions.
2) Notify CS and publish incident stub with preliminary impact assessment.
3) Revert infra changes if root cause is configuration.
4) Postmortem within 72 hours if rollback executed.

Telemetry sampling plan (reduce noise, maximize signal):
- Sampling windows: full sampling for platinum customers, 10% sampling for enterprise, 1% for standard outside canary buckets.
- Key metrics to watch:
  - p50/p95/p99 latency by model variant + region (1m granularity).
  - Error rate (4xx/5xx split) by route and customer tier (30s granularity).
  - CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, batching size distribution.
  - Request queue length and backpressure counters on serving nodes.
  - Token generation time per-step for long-context calls.
- Quick diagnostics queries (to run from SRE console):
  - top_errors(last_15m) grouped by route
  - p99_latency_by_shard(last_5m)
  - cache_hit_ratio_over_time(last_30m)
- Runbook note: capture 1m histograms and persist for 72h (for postmortem correlation).

Customer impact matrix (concise):
Columns: Customer tier | Region(s) | Expected exposure during canary | Primary impact surface
- Platinum | NA, EU | 0% (fallback lane) initially | API latency sensitivity; SLA breach risk
- Enterprise | NA, EU, APAC | 1–5% early ramps | Bulk inference throughput, tail latency
- Standard | Global | included in later ramps (15–70%) | Best-effort latency, ephemeral errors tolerated
Notes: If an enterprise customer reports >2% error rate delta from baseline in the first 2h, pause expansion for that customer's shard/placement and engage solutions engineering.

Release notes (draft to share with CS/AM preflight):
Title: OptiBatch v2.3 rollout (Mar 2026) — improved batching heuristics and KV cache tuning
Summary: This release tweaks the serving runtime's batching policy to favor smaller, more frequent batches for low-latency routes, and adjusts KV cache eviction thresholds to reduce cache churn on high-concurrency workloads. Expected outcome is modest p50 improvement for chat-style flows and lower tail latency variability for medium-length contexts.
Notable changes:
- Serving runtime: adaptive batch sizing algorithm updated (optibatch-v2.3).
- Cache: eviction policy relaxed to increase cache TTL for recent prefixes.
- Config: default per-tenant max_batch_delay reduced from 12ms to 8ms for latency-sensitive routes.
Impact and mitigations:
- Potential increase in GPU utilization (2–6%) under heavy sustained throughput; autoscaling profiles adjusted to account for this.
- Enterprise customers with very large batched workloads may see small throughput regressions; teams should validate bulk-predict pipelines.
Known issues (pre-flight):
- Observed intermittent +10% p99 drift in an internal stress test when KV cache warmed from cold for very long-sequence inputs (investigating).
- Rare 429s on a legacy rate-limiter path (mitigation: route to fallback).
Rollout notes for CS/AM: share the above customer-impact matrix and the tentative timeline. Ask platinum customers if they want a dedicated dry-run window.

Post-rollout checklist (T+24h and T+72h):
- [ ] Confirm 72h histogram persistence and archive.
- [ ] Run post-deploy quality evals against the canonical prompt set (quality/regression checks).
- [ ] Gather CS feedback for platinum/enterprise engagements.
- [ ] If no regressions and error budget intact, mark release as "final" and update release tag.
- [ ] If rollback executed, schedule incident triage and blameless postmortem within 72h.

Appendix: quick comm templates
- Immediate incident stub (short):
  Title: OptiBatch v2.3 — automated rollback executed for region EU at T+0:45
  Summary: Automated SLO gate triggered due to sustained p99 delta +36% over baseline. Canary paused and traffic reverted. Engineering investigating; CS notified.
- Customer-facing note (CS):
  Subject: Brief outage notice — OptiBatch rollout paused
  Body: Hi <Name>, we observed an automated safety rollback during a planned rollout. Your traffic was not impacted beyond the rollback; we are investigating and will provide an update within 2 hours.

Open items for the release owner:
- Confirm final canary buckets (IPs / tenant-ids) and ensure mapping file is checked into release artifacts.
- Decide whether to allow a 1-hour dedicated platinum dry-run (requires manual opt-in).
- Validate autoscaler headroom for expected 6% utilization bump.

End of runbook (draft). Please add comments inline to this doc prior to the final preflight meeting.
